name: crandel
author: clothes-dressing-packing designer
description: Washing hanging on lines, drawn small. CLUE: ONE GROUP PER LINE, separated by "/", e.g. `321/531/2` = three washing lines. Group i is `<rows><longs><drips>`: `rows` = how many rows of air hang under that line (2-6, 8-12 in all, 3 or 4 lines), `longs` = how many garments on that line hang ALL THE WAY DOWN to the line below, `drips` = how many of THOSE have a garment hanging directly underneath them (their columns overlap). The LAST group is a single digit: the bottom line has nothing below it, so it carries only its row count. drips < longs always (and longs - drips <= 2), so every line always shows at least one long garment hanging over a bare stretch. SOLUTION: an ASCII drying rack, every row the same width (the drawer picks 20-28). A row whose characters are only "=" and "v" is a LINE ("v" = a peg, cosmetic and unchecked); every other row is air. A GARMENT is a horizontal run of one capital letter hanging from the line above: it must appear in the top row of its block and the identical run must repeat down to its hem, so garments are rectangles and each row's runs are a subset of the row above. Everything else - filler char, letters, widths, hems, pegs, how many garments - is free. The scorer rebuilds the clue from the picture (rows per line; long garments per line; how many of those overlap a garment of the next line) and compares strings. PRIVATE - INTENDED DISCOVERY PATH: one demo gives "washing on lines"; the grammar is rebuilt in 1-2 demos; the FIRST digit of each group is readable straight off the picture (count the rows) and is what tells a solver that a group belongs to a line; the SECOND digit ("how many hang right down to the next line") is the foothold and is guessable from one demo - getting it alone and choosing the drippers at random scores 10.8%, a real improving signal rather than a wall of zeros; the THIRD digit is the lateral step. It is a subset of the long ones, and the two neighbouring readings are dead on arrival: "all the long ones" IS the second digit, so it is visibly not the third; "the ones with something underneath" (short ones included) is falsified on every line of every demo. What is left is the conjunction a 12-year-old says out loud: that towel is so long it touches the next line, AND it is dripping on the shirt under it. solve() throws away any picture in which any of 12 rival per-line readouts equals the drip vector (all-with-something-below, garments, short, short-with-something-below, wide, fully-covering, over-two, long-and-wide, long-and-narrow, long-not-at-either-end, pairs, distinct-garments-dripped-on). WITNESS TABLE (250 fresh clues; every attacker knows the grammar AND the first two digits, and differs only in the law it uses for the third; each draws in its own naive style): true rule 100%; "in the left half" 12.4%; "wide" 12.4%; "not at either end" 12.0%; "narrow" 11.6%; "fully covers something below" 11.3%; random choice among the long ones 10.8%; "hangs over two" 2.0%. TEMPLATES: identical garment columns on every line (this scored 87% against a one-digit-per-line version) 0.0%; two garments a line 0.0%; a picture with the right rows but random hems (row counts only) 0.0%; previous answer replayed 0.0%; one fixed answer for every clue 0.8%; empty/junk/clue echoed 0.0% (20000 junk strings: 0 raises, 0 non-binary, 0 false positives, worst score() 0.13 ms). ~6500 distinct clue classes; brute-force-and-cache over 6x450 probes is worth ~18% of the final on top of the ~11% blind rate, i.e. the no-insight ceiling is ~26%. HYPOTHESIS ELIMINATION: over a family of 150 per-line readouts, 6.5 survive one demo, 1.7 survive two, and the true rule is the ONLY survivor after 5 demos in 30/30 trials. v2 (2026-09-04, kid-legibility pass after a 2.6/5 judge score): the clue was regrouped from three fields (`gaps/longs/drips`) to one group per line so its shape matches the picture; racks narrowed from 26-32 to 20-28 with 3-6 garments a line, every garment 2-6 columns wide with air beside it and pegs drawn over it; a dripping garment now overlaps the washing below by >= 2 columns and a non-dripping long one clears everything below by >= 2 columns, so the drip is a picture (an unbroken column of washing through the line) instead of a column-alignment computation. Author: clothes/dressing/packing direction.
